verified: A negotiated events.checkpoint.v1 stream can validate Last-Event-ID together with X-Iris-After-Event-ID in the same read snapshot used for its successors
A visible anchor survives numeric gaps caused by tenant filtering; a verified head returns an empty finite SSE stream
Missing, changed or inaccessible saved anchors return JSON HTTP 410 history_unavailable with retryable=false before SSE headers, without revealing actual event identities
Out-of-range cursors and an identity without a positive cursor fail before streaming; SDK rejects invalid new checkpoint inputs before fetch
Disabled SSE removes both capabilities; fresh trusted initialization credentials include the new checkpoint capability
Legacy cursor-only requests retain their response behavior; the SDK forwards the optional identity and rejects both 410 and 503 as errors rather than empty polls
Reviewed public API changes are limited to streamEvents contract digest and the optional afterEventId TypeScript parameter
limits: This is source-level Core ASGI/packaging/local HTTP and SDK transport coverage. The installed Bellis SDK 0.11.1 and prior Core wheel have not been replaced or claimed to support the new capability
The anchor proves only that the last accepted visible event can still be located; it does not cryptographically prove the full log or detect arbitrary removal of other events
Bellis still needs durable cursor/event identity, a history-unavailable read and delivery barrier, public full revalidation and old-snapshot recovery tests
No full Core regression, new installed-wheel integration, A3 gap recovery, A4 matrix or Phase4B completion claim is made
